standard.purpose: Deposit covers manufacturing commitment and reduces TCD exposure to client default

largeProjects.structure: 30% deposit / 30% on production completion / 40% on delivery
largeProjects.purpose: Milestone payments align client payments with TCD's own payment obligations to supplier

paymentStructure.never: 100% prepayment before manufacture — creates buyer friction and is non-standard in the industry

typical50kProject.day5: Supplier payment due: 30% of supplier cost ≈ $8,000–$10,000
typical50kProject.week8: Final supplier payment and freight invoice settled

cashflowTimeline.exposurePeriod: TCD typically carries 4–8 weeks of cash exposure between deposit payment to supplier and receiving balance from client — manage timing carefully on multiple concurrent projects

clientCashflowSensitivity.commonObjection: Many clients are not objecting to the price — they are objecting to the cash flow impact of a large upfront payment
solutions: Finance option (12–60 month terms) — converts large upfront to monthly outflow
Milestone payment structure — aligns furniture payments with client's own cash cycle
EOFY timing — position purchase before June 30 for immediate tax deduction
clientCashflowSensitivity.EOFYPositioning: Commercial furniture is a depreciable asset. Purchasing before June 30 allows a full-year depreciation claim — a real financial benefit. Use this from April onward.
clientCashflowSensitivity.financePositioning: Finance converts a $120,000 capital decision into a $2,800/month operating expense — dramatically changes the CFO's approval threshold

creditorManagement.supplierTerms: Most Foshan suppliers require 30% deposit at order, 70% against Bill of Lading
creditorManagement.freightBroker: Freight broker typically requires prepayment or credit facility — establish credit early
creditorManagement.installationContractors: Pay installation contractors within 7 days of completion — good contractors are in demand and cash flow is their primary concern
